trick: Colonial education was designed to produce clerks, and the national education movement was the answer to that. Every institution in this chapter exists because Indians wanted science and technical training the government would not provide.

video.query: national education movement technical education Bengal class 10 history

data.prompt: True or false? Mark each statement.

items.statement: Macaulay's Minute of 1835 favoured English education over Indian learning.
items.why: It argued for producing a class Indian in blood but English in taste, and set the direction of colonial education for a century.

items.statement: The Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science was founded by Mahendralal Sarkar.
items.why: Founded in 1876, it was the first institution in India devoted to original scientific research by Indians.

items.statement: The Bengal Technical Institute grew out of the Swadeshi movement.
items.why: The national education movement of 1905–06 created it, and it later became Jadavpur University.

items.statement: Calcutta University was founded in the twentieth century.
items.why: It was founded in 1857, along with Bombay and Madras, on the recommendation of Wood's Despatch of 1854.

items.statement: The Serampore College was set up by the British government.
items.why: It was founded in 1818 by the Baptist missionaries Carey, Marshman and Ward, not by the government.
